name: Wishlist Kit Lite – Wishlist Plugin for WordPress and WooCommerce
author: Abdul Wahab Taqi

sections.description:
Wishlist Kit Lite lets visitors save items for later without requiring a separate service account. It works with public WordPress posts, pages, and enabled public post types. WooCommerce and Elementor are optional integrations, not requirements.

Features included in this plugin:

  • Guest and signed-in wishlists, with named lists and a default list.
  • Guest lists transfer to the visitor’s account when they sign in on the same browser.
  • Private lists and a responsive table view with search, sorting, and incremental loading.
  • Move items between lists and remove selected items.
  • WooCommerce product prices, stock status, and individual or selected-item cart actions where the product can be purchased without further choices.
  • Configurable button placement and saved-heart fill color. The default outline heart has a border and background.
  • Shortcodes, two dynamic blocks, and optional Elementor widgets.
  • Administrator-only collection overview and WordPress personal-data export and erasure integration.

No license key, purchase, time limit, or external account is required for these features. Email alerts, reports, advanced organization, list and grid layouts, advanced theme customization and social sharing belong to the separate Wishlist Pro add-on. Lite includes informational Pro pages, not the implementation of those features.

Protected, unpublished, password-protected, and unavailable items are not exposed to unauthorized visitors. Optional DownloadsKit integration respects the current viewer’s access and uses its delivery URL rather than exposing a file storage path.

External services

No external API or remotely hosted script is required. Product and content images use the URLs supplied by your site and its media configuration.

The free plugin does not contact social-sharing services, send stock alerts or send marketing email.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the wishlist-kit-lite folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or upload the ZIP using Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Wishlist Kit Lite.
  3. Open Wishlist > Settings and choose which public content types can be saved.
  4. Select an existing published page containing [wishlistkit_lite], or click Create Page. Creating a page requires an explicit administrator action.
  5. Save settings. Choose automatic button placement or add a save button manually.
  6. Visit the page and save an item to test your configuration.

Manual shortcodes:

  • [wishlistkit_lite] displays the wishlist workspace.
  • [wishlistkit_lite_button] displays a save button for the current item.
  • [wishlistkit_lite_button id=”123″] targets a public, enabled item by ID.
  • [wishlistkit_lite_counter] displays the visitor’s saved-item count.

The block editor provides Wishlist and Save to wishlist blocks. Elementor, when installed, provides Wishlist and Save to Wishlist widgets. JavaScript and the site’s REST API must be available for interactive saving.
sections.faq:
Does this work without WooCommerce or Pro?

Yes. Visitors can save enabled public WordPress content and manage their lists with this plugin alone. Product and cart actions appear only when WooCommerce is available.

What happens to variable products?

Products needing additional options must be opened to choose them. The plugin does not bypass WooCommerce purchase, stock, or cart validation.

Are wishlists public?

No. The free plugin has no public-sharing endpoint or sharing strip. Sharing requires the separate Pro add-on. Disabling Pro removes access to its sharing endpoints without deleting stored collections or customization settings.

What data and cookies are stored?

The plugin stores list names, ownership references, visibility, item references, and dates in custom tables in your site’s database. Guest saving uses a random, HTTP-only wishlistkit_lite_guest cookie with a 30-day lifetime; a hash identifies guest lists in the database. Signed-in lists use the WordPress user ID. Guest lists not updated for 30 days are deleted by a daily WordPress scheduled task. Scheduled cleanup depends on WP-Cron running.

The plugin does not start PHP sessions or send analytics to WPKits. Account export and erasure use WordPress’s privacy tools. Suggested privacy-policy text is available in WordPress’s privacy settings.

What happens on deactivation or uninstall?

Deactivation stops the plugin’s scheduled guest cleanup and retains collections. Uninstall retains data by default to avoid accidental loss. To permanently remove this plugin’s tables and settings, back up first and add define( ‘WISHLISTKIT_LITE_REMOVE_DATA’, true ); to wp-config.php before deleting the plugin. The configured WordPress page is retained.

Can I use it on a multisite network?

Activate and manage the plugin separately on each site. Collections belong to that site’s database tables. Network-wide migration and network-wide data erasure are not provided.

Can I import an existing WooKit wishlist?

An administrator-only WP-CLI staging importer is included for local, development, or staging environments. It is not an automatic live migration. Back up both systems and freeze source writes first. Run wp wishlistkit-lite import preview –user=ADMIN, then use the reported fingerprint with the start, batch, and verify operations. See wp help wishlistkit-lite import for arguments. The importer leaves legacy tables unchanged and never switches the live runtime. Guest browser credentials are not migrated automatically.
sections.changelog:
1.1.20

  • Every visitor now has a default list, named “Favorites”. It is offered first in the “Choose a list” dialog, even before the visitor has created any list, and is created the first time it is used.
  • New setting: Default list name (General tab). Sites still using the old default name “Wishlist” are switched to “Favorites”; custom names are kept.
  • Fix: the heart now shows as saved on shop pages (and on a product page before a variation is chosen) when any variation of that product is in a wishlist. Before, items saved as a specific size or colour looked unsaved after a page reload.
  • Consistent wording on the wishlist page: the tab is now “My wishlists” (was “Your wishlists”), matching the “My Wishlist” title.
  • Choosing a product variation on the wishlist page updates the item in place, without the list disappearing and reloading.
  • Placement settings are now self-explanatory: clearer names, a one-line description for every setting and a live explanation of the selected option, plus how to place the button by hand with the shortcode, block or Elementor widget.

1.1.19

  • Use Wishlist Kit Lite specific public prefixes and namespace.
  • Remove Astra-specific placement handling from the Lite package.

1.1.18

  • Sanitize filtered inline CSS rules before output.

1.1.17

  • Update the plugin URL to match the Wishlist Kit Lite slug.

1.1.15

  • Update the WordPress.org contributor username in the readme.

1.1.14

  • Update Lite release metadata, author details, plugin URL and WordPress.org repository title.

0.1.14

  • Add documented WordPress.org scanner suppressions for intentional plugin-owned custom-table operations.
  • Rebuild the submission package after the Plugin Check warning cleanup.
  • Refresh the companion Pro dependency target.

0.1.13

  • Rename the Lite package to Wishlist Kit Lite with the matching wishlist-kit-lite slug, main file and text domain.
  • Keep existing wishlist data, REST routes, WP-CLI import commands and storage identifiers stable during the rename.
  • Refresh the companion Pro dependency target.

0.1.11

  • Prepare the initial directory submission with matching package slug and text domain.
  • Add setup, privacy, external-sharing, and data-retention documentation.
  • Separate Pro email-editor assets and settings from the free package.
  • Make existing selected-item cart actions available without an upgrade gate.
  • Correct JavaScript translation extraction and editor translation loading.
  • Restore access to additional saved items and keep bulk requests bounded.
  • Harden optional download access and request validation.

upgrade_notice.1.1.20: Adds a default "Favorites" list for every visitor (name editable in Settings > General) and clearer placement settings.
upgrade_notice.1.1.19: Advanced themes, list/grid layouts and sharing now require the separate Wishlist Pro 0.1.13 add-on. Back up existing development installations. Existing settings and collections are retained. Never activate both an earlier development folder and wishlist-kit-lite at once.
